ESA narrowband electromagnetic interference reference limit (paragraph 6.6.2.1.): in the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz the limit E shall be 53 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth.

requirements.text: The measurement of broadband electromagnetic emissions from ESAs shall be performed according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 7.
During the broadband emission test (Annex 7), the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
For ESAs other than those involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
The broadband emission limits for ESAs apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

The ESA broadband emission limits of paragraphs 6.5. and 7.10. are for quasi-peak detectors; measurements may be performed with quasi-peak or peak detectors, and if peak detectors are used a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
The measurement of narrowband electromagnetic emissions from ESAs shall be performed according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 8.
During the narrowband emission test (Annex 8), the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
The ESA narrowband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.
The narrowband emission limits for ESAs apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
ESA narrowband emission measurements shall be performed with an average detector.

ESAs other than those in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid' may comply with the immunity requirements using any combination of the absorber chamber test (ISO 11452-2), TEM cell test (ISO 11452-3), bulk current injection test (ISO 11452-4), stripline test (ISO 11452-5) and reverberation chamber test (ISO 11452-11) at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9 is covered.
The ESA immunity test conditions, including frequency range and general test conditions, shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
During the ESA immunity test, the ESA under test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
ESA immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps, step size and dwell time chosen according to ISO 11452-1.

In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be AM with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the ESA immunity test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
The ESA absorber chamber immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-2 using the substitution method to establish the test field conditions, with vertical polarization.
The ESA TEM cell immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3, with maximum field coupling to the ESA or to the wiring harness inside the TEM cell depending on the ESA to be tested.

The ESA bulk current injection immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench, using either the substitution method with the injection probe at 150 mm from the ESA or the closed loop method with the injection probe at 900 mm from the ESA.

As an alternative, the ESA may be tested for bulk current injection immunity while installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4, using the substitution method with the injection probe at 150 mm from the ESA.
The ESA stripline immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
The ESA reverberation chamber immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11, unless otherwise specified using a test setup with ground plane.
ESAs shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply, and conducted transients from ESAs to the vehicle power supply shall be limited, as tested according to Annex 10.
Test pulse 1 according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of ESAs and to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
Test pulse 2a according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of ESAs and to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
Test pulse 2b according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of ESAs and to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
Test pulse 3a according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of ESAs and to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
Test pulse 3b according to ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of ESAs and to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines of ESAs and to other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines; ESAs exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12 V/24 V starter motor) are not subject to the starting profile.

Emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 on supply lines and on other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The external surface of vehicles shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision.
The external surface of vehicles shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.

No protruding part of the external surface shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm; this does not apply to parts protruding less than 5 mm, but the outward facing angles of such parts shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.

Protruding parts of the external surface made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A may have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm; the hardness shall be measured with the component as installed on the vehicle, and where a Shore A measurement is impossible, comparable measurements shall be used for evaluation.
The provisions of paragraphs 5.1. to 5.5. shall apply in addition to the particular specifications of paragraph 6., except where these particular specifications expressly provide otherwise.
Vehicles (separate technical units) approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 5. and 6.

The dimension of the projection of a component mounted on a convex external surface may be determined either directly or by reference to a drawing of an appropriate section of the component in its installed condition.

If the dimension of the projection of a component mounted on a surface other than convex cannot be determined by simple measurement, it shall be determined as the maximum variation of the distance of the centre of a 100 mm diameter sphere from the nominal line of the panel when the sphere is moved over and is in constant contact with that component (Figure 3).
